CHRISTOPHE PRINCE
OT Network Security Operations Dashboard
v0.7 · User Guide

A standalone browser-based tool for OT/ICS network traffic analysis. No installation, no backend, no internet connection required — load a .pcap or .pcapng file and get instant visibility into your industrial network.

Designed for use during IEC 62443 security audit missions. All processing happens locally in your browser via a background Web Worker — the UI stays responsive even on large captures.

Standalone HTML No backend pcap/pcapng IEC 62443 Multi-VLAN OT/ICS DPI Web Worker streaming
01 Quick Start
📂
Load capture files
Click Open file or drag & drop one or more .pcap / .pcapng files. Name files with VLAN hints (e.g. VLAN20_OT.pcap) for automatic segment detection. Multiple files are merged into a unified view.
VLANs, 802.1Q tags and Flows picker
When the file name gives the VLAN (V10.pcap, vlan20_…), that VLAN is used and 802.1Q tags inside the file are not turned into extra VLANs (a notice in the bottom bar lists them). Use the 802.1Q selector in the top bar to force tag-based VLANs. In Flows, type or pick an IP (sorted list) to filter, and switch the sort to IP. In Topology, whitelisted IPs automatically reveal the nodes they talk to (green rings, including same-VLAN peers); toggle with the Whitelist peers chip.
🎬
Try demo data
Click Demo to load a pre-built 6-VLAN industrial scenario with inter-zone crossings, external communications, Modbus writes and behavioral alerts — no file needed.
📄
Export your report
Click PDF to generate a professional audit report. In Chrome/Edge: Print → Save as PDF. The report includes device fingerprints, findings, host inventory, inter-VLAN matrix and IEC 62443 recommendations.
02 Top Bar
Risk Badge
Global risk: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW — computed from external comms, unknown IPs and zone crossings.
KPI Pills
Hosts · Unknown IPs · Inter-VLAN · External — click any pill to filter the Flows panel. Hover for details.
Status Indicator
Shows parse progress (⟳ file.pcap · 45%), then ✓ Ready or ⚠ N critical. Click when red/orange to jump to Analysis tab.
Theme / PDF / Help
Toggle dark/light theme (all panels adapt including topology canvas). Generate PDF report. Open this user guide.
03 Navigation Tabs
Matrix

Inter-VLAN traffic heatmap. Rows = source VLAN, columns = destination. Cell color = byte volume (green → orange → red). Purple cells = traffic involving unknown IPs. Use this view to spot unexpected cross-zone communications instantly.

Topology

Purdue Model layout. Zones detected automatically from VLAN names (Enterprise, DMZ, Control, Field, Untrusted).

  • Zone order — Internet / External sits above Enterprise, outside the Purdue model; multicast and broadcast groups stay inside their local VLAN
  • External nodes — public destinations grouped by Threat Intel actor (Apple, Google, Microsoft…) or by /24 prefix, with an overflow node beyond 12 groups
  • Node icons — PLC/RTU (square+dot), HMI (screen), Server (rack), Firewall (shield), Workstation (monitor), DNS/NTP (globe)
  • Curved links — thickness proportional to byte volume, colour by protocol. A link is drawn only when both endpoints resolve to a real node, so no arrow ever ends in empty space
  • Protocol labels — shown on every link when the graph is small, otherwise only for the hovered or selected node
  • Dashed red links — zone crossing or external traffic · Pulsing red ring — node has alerts
  • Click node — highlights it and its peers, filters Flows panel · Hover node — full tooltip with vendor/model if fingerprinted
  • Click a flow row — switches to Topology and selects the source node
Scope

Topology limited to your whitelist. Every IP or CIDR range added in the Whitelist tab appears here, with only the links between whitelisted assets. Use it for a readable view of a large capture — Topology keeps the full, dense picture.

A small orange badge on a node counts its inter-VLAN flows. Click a node for its peers, ports and volumes.

Whitelist

Known asset registry. Add IP addresses or CIDR ranges (e.g. 192.168.20.0/24) that are authorized. IPs not in the whitelist are flagged UNKNOWN everywhere and generate alerts.

Threat Intel

IP classification engine. Built-in database: Google/Cloudflare DNS, Microsoft/Azure, AWS, GitHub, Telegram, Tor (CRITICAL), multicast, NTP. Add custom entries with IP/CIDR, name, category and risk level — persists in localStorage.

Analysis

Deep audit view — two columns:

  • Host Inventory — every host with device type, vendor/model (if fingerprinted via EtherNet/IP), traffic, protocols, open ports, OT command history, and complete "Communicates with" list with all peers, ports and services. No truncation.
  • Security Findings — CRITICAL / WARNING / INFO badges, BEHAVIORAL / FINGERPRINT categories, evidence details (register addresses, S7 function names, CIP services, sequences).
Scope Analysis

Analysis restricted to the whitelisted assets. Same layout as Analysis: host inventory on the left, security findings on the right — but only for the assets in scope and the findings that involve at least one of them.

  • Each asset lists every peer it talks to, marked in scope or out of scope; the header counts the out-of-scope peers contacted
  • Findings that concern only out-of-scope hosts are hidden and counted (see the Analysis tab for the full list)
  • Updates as soon as the Whitelist changes
04 Flows Panel (Right Column)

Lists all detected flows — no limit. Critical flows (external, unknown IPs) always surfaced first. Sorted by volume.

05 Traffic Timeline

Stacked bar chart — bars colored by VLAN, external traffic in red. Hover a bar: intra-VLAN volume, inter-VLAN flows (V→V + protocol + KB), external flows, top talker for that interval.

Click a bar — time filter: active flows ranked first, inactive dimmed, critical flows always visible. Click the yellow badge or the bar again to clear.

06 Detection Capabilities
Network Alerts
CRITICAL External communications from internal hosts
CRITICAL Unknown source IP on network
CRITICAL Zone crossing: untrusted/guest → OT control zone
CRITICAL Malicious IP (Tor, flagged Threat Intel)
Behavioral Detection
WARNING Port scan / host sweep (≥8 destinations)
WARNING Unusual protocol in OT zone (HTTP, DNS, RDP…)
WARNING Asymmetric traffic — possible exfiltration (ratio >10×)
WARNING Excessive broadcast (>50 packets / >100 KB)
WARNING Cleartext protocols: Telnet, FTP, HTTP
WARNING OT device mixing OT and IT protocols
WARNING Unknown external IP (not in Threat Intel)
WARNING Slow reconnaissance — many hosts over >5 min, low bytes
Advanced OT Analysis
CRITICAL Unauthorized Modbus write from IT/untrusted zone — with register addresses and write counts
WARNING Register flood — same register written >50 times
CRITICAL Write to register 0 with value 0 (device reset/stop command)
WARNING Industrial cycle anomaly — gap >5× normal polling interval
WARNING Possible replay attack — identical OT command repeated >10×
DPI Critical Commands
CRITICAL S7 PLC Stop (function 0x29)
CRITICAL S7 Request Download / Download Block / Download Ended (0x1A–0x1C) — program written to the PLC
CRITICAL S7 PLC Control (0x28): activate block _INSE · delete block _DELE · start/stop program P_PROGRAM
WARNING S7 Start Upload / Upload / End Upload (0x1D–0x1F) — program read from the PLC · Write Var (0x05) · other PLC Control services
CRITICAL S7 sequence program download followed by block activation, program start or CPU stop on the same PLC
CRITICAL DNP3 Operate / Direct Operate / Direct Operate No Ack (FC 0x04–0x06) — physical output control
CRITICAL DNP3 Cold / Warm Restart (0x0D / 0x0E) · Initialize Data / Application (0x0F / 0x10) · Start / Stop Application (0x11 / 0x12)
CRITICAL EtherNet/IP CIP Reset (service 0x05) · Stop (0x07) — direct requests
WARNING EtherNet/IP CIP Write Tag (0x4D / 0x53) · Start (0x06) · Execute PCCC (0x4B) — direct requests
CRITICAL FINS (Omron) CPU Stop/Start · Memory Write
CRITICAL Modbus FC8 Diagnostics/Restart · FC43 Device Identification (reconnaissance)
Device Fingerprinting (EtherNet/IP List Identity)
INFO Allen-Bradley / Rockwell — Vendor ID 1 · product name read from the device itself (e.g. "1756-L85E/B LOGIX5585")
INFO Schneider Electric (Vendor ID 243) · Omron (47) — IDs verified against ODVA records
INFO Any other vendor — the raw Vendor ID is shown together with the product name the device reports
INFO Device type (PLC, AC drive, HMI, communications adapter, generic) · Revision · Serial number
INFO Mitsubishi MELSEC (port 5006/5007) · Omron FINS (port 9600)
07 OT Protocol Deep Parsing

The parser reads beyond TCP/UDP into the application layer. Extracted data drives fingerprinting, critical command detection and behavioral analysis.

MODBUS TCP · Port 502
Function Code, Unit ID, register address & value (FC5/6/15/16), register count (FC1-4). Critical: FC8 Diagnostics/Restart, FC43 Device Identification.
S7 / S7COMM · Port 102
TPKT/COTP/S7 parsed. Function code read from the parameter block: program download (0x1A–0x1C), upload (0x1D–0x1F), PLC Control (0x28, service names _INSE / _DELE / P_PROGRAM), PLC Stop (0x29), Write Var (0x05). Download → activation/stop sequence detection.
DNP3 · Port 20000
Start bytes (0x05 0x64), little-endian addresses, function code of the first fragment. Operate / Direct Operate, Cold/Warm Restart, Initialize, Start/Stop Application detected.
EtherNet/IP · Port 44818
List Identity (command 0x0063, little-endian): Vendor ID, Device Type, Product Name, revision, serial. CIP requests in SendRRData / SendUnitData: Write Tag (0x4D/0x53), Reset / Start / Stop (0x05/0x06/0x07), Execute PCCC (0x4B).
FINS (Omron) · Port 9600
Command codes extracted. Memory Write, CPU Stop, CPU Start detected as critical.
MELSEC (Mitsubishi) · Port 5006/7
Protocol detection from magic bytes. Vendor identified as Mitsubishi Electric.

09 PDF Audit Report

Click PDF → Chrome/Edge: Print → Save as PDF. The report is generated entirely from captured data — no data leaves the browser.

Cover + Executive Summary
Mission name, date, risk badge, 6 KPIs, network segment table with Purdue zones and alert status, top critical findings.
Inter-VLAN Matrix
Color-coded traffic matrix + external communications table with Threat Intel classification, source IPs, protocols and volumes.
Security Findings
All CRITICAL/WARNING/INFO findings with BEHAVIORAL/FINGERPRINT badges, evidence (register writes, S7 function names, CIP services, sequences).
Host Inventory
Hosts grouped by VLAN. Each host: type, Purdue zone, traffic, protocols, open ports, EtherNet/IP identity (vendor, model, revision, serial) or OT fingerprint, findings, peer list with ports/services.
Recommendations
Personalized IEC 62443 recommendations based on detected findings — Security Level SL-1/2/3 with priority LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL.
Disclaimer
Based on passive traffic analysis only. Does not constitute a formal IEC 62443 Security Level assessment or penetration test.
10 Tips & Limitations

Best practices

  • Name files with VLAN IDs: vlan20_ot.pcap, V30_field.pcapng
  • Load multiple files simultaneously — all merged into one view
  • Add authorized IP ranges to Whitelist before analyzing to reduce false positives
  • Add mission-specific IPs (VPN gateways, jump servers) to Threat Intel with appropriate risk
  • For EtherNet/IP fingerprinting, ensure the capture includes UDP port 44818 discovery traffic
  • Use the Analysis tab as the primary audit view — Flows is for investigation
  • Large files (>800 MB) are processed in 64 MB chunks via Web Worker — the UI stays responsive

Known limitations

  • IPv6 traffic is not parsed
  • Encrypted payloads (TLS, SSH) cannot be inspected — metadata only
  • OT DPI requires unencrypted protocols on standard ports
  • EtherNet/IP fingerprinting requires List Identity packets in the capture (not always present in operational captures)
  • EtherNet/IP: only vendor IDs verified against ODVA records are named (Rockwell 1, Omron 47, Schneider 243); CIP services are read from direct requests, not from Unconnected_Send wrappers
  • Protocol decoders follow the published specifications and are verified on synthetic packets — please report any mismatch seen on real captures
  • S7: the exact CPU model is not available passively (it needs SZL Read responses), and the negotiated PDU size cannot reliably tell an S7-1200 from an S7-1500
  • Multicast / broadcast destinations may still be reported as external in some alerts — Topology and Scope place them in their local VLAN
  • pcapng streaming: chunks accumulated then parsed at end (pcap streaming is chunk-by-chunk)
  • If the browser blocks Web Workers (e.g. Safari opening a local file://), the dashboard automatically falls back to a synchronous parser — slower on very large files but fully functional
